spec.hypothesis: Holding SPY scaled each month end to a 15% annualized volatility target (weight = min(1, 0.15 / realized volatility of the last 21 trading days), the rest in T-bills, no leverage) delivers a Sharpe ratio at least equal to buy-and-hold SPY with a maximum drawdown at least 5 percentage points shallower.
spec.rationale: Equity volatility clusters while expected returns do not rise proportionally, so cutting exposure when recent volatility is high has historically improved risk-adjusted returns (Moreira and Muir 2017; Harvey, Hoyle, Korgaonkar, Rattray, Sargaison and Van Hemert 2018). Out-of-sample evidence is mixed (Cederburg, O'Doherty, Wang and Yan 2020), and without leverage most of any benefit should come from smaller drawdowns rather than higher returns, so a modest result is expected. This uses the time-series volatility of one index ETF; it is unrelated to the closed cross-sectional stock features in research/policy.json (rank_volatility, rank_volatility_63). The 2017-2026 window contains two sharp drawdowns (2020, 2022), which is where the rule should matter.

signal.description: annualized standard deviation of SPY daily returns over the last 21 trading days

spec.decision_rule: If every gate passes: freeze as qualified and forward-test for 24 months against SPY on Sharpe. If any gate fails: close H7; do not try other volatility targets, lookbacks, caps or leverage on this data.
